subject: NimbleHealth pricing follow-up — $/1M token targets & benchmarking
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Trent <michael.trent@nimblehealth.com>; Jessica Lin <jessica.lin@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: NimbleHealth discovery — unit economics & target $/1M

Hi Michael & Jessica,

Thanks again for a great conversation today — appreciate the clarity on the three main workloads (triage summaries, customer Q&A, and internal search embeddings). As promised, I wanted to capture the high-level numbers we discussed and outline next steps.

Quick bullet summary from our call:
- Monthly active users: ~18k (mostly support agents peak 9a–6p PT)
- Estimated token mix: 60% prompts, 40% responses; avg prompt 120 tokens, avg response 220 tokens
- Expected steady-state monthly tokens: ~850M tokens (projected Q3 baseline)
- Q2 pilot target: 80–120M tokens (1–2 months)
- Budget range discussed for pilot: $1.5k–$6k per month (tbd based on SLA/throughput)

Competitive benchmark: you asked how Redwood compares to OpenAI/Anthropic and popular open-model hosts on $/1M token economics. High level: we can show competitive unit pricing when customers move to Redwood Dedicated or optimized quantized runtimes; hosted plan parity depends on model choice and SLA. I attached a quick comparison PDF with example $/1M numbers across small-to-medium throughput profiles.

Action items / asks:
1) Can you share the Q2 usage estimate file you referenced so we can validate the token split and peaks? (I attached our template to the reply thread.)
2) Michael — confirm whether the procurement cadence prefers a single pilot PO or incremental SOWs.
3) Ben / Sergio — can you propose two target $/1M price points we could present for the pilot (conservative and stretch), and note which deployment (hosted/dedicated/private) those map to?

I'll regroup internally once I have the Nimble usage sheet and the procurement preference.

Thanks,
Irene
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_price_comparison.pdf (PDF, 240KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Michael Trent <michael.trent@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: NimbleHealth discovery — unit economics & target $/1M

Irene — thanks for the recap. Quick notes from pricing side:

- Pilot pricing (80–120M tokens): recommend two options:
  * Hosted Pilot (fastest): $1.80 / 1M tokens (includes basic SLA, best-effort throughput); expect ~5–7ms additional latency vs. Dedicated.
  * Dedicated Preview (reserved small pool): $0.95 / 1M tokens (committed baseline + small overage); requires 3–6 month commitment for cost to amortize.

- For steady-state (~850M/mo), target competitive tiers we can propose: $0.65–$0.85 / 1M on Dedicated (depends on quantization & batching); open-host equivalents we measured: OpenAI gpt-4x-like hosts ~ $1.8–2.2 / 1M (managed), Anthropic equivalents ~ $1.6–2.0 / 1M. Note: open-model self-hosted costs can be lower on GPU-heavy sustained loads but require ops.

- Attachments: I ran a quick model-config sensitivity and attached the one-pager "nimble_q2_usage_estimate.xlsx" template — fills will help us compute sample monthly spend under each price.

I'll follow up with a short table tying the $/1M targets to expected monthly spend for the two pilot sizes.

-Ben
Senior Growth — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: nimble_q2_usage_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Trent <michael.trent@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: NimbleHealth discovery — unit economics & target $/1M

Adding a few commercial context points for negotiation and benchmarking:

- If Nimble wants pilot elasticity (spiky peaks during support hours) with minimal operational lift, recommend Hosted Pilot at $1.80/1M with a throughput burst SLA. That maps to the lowest friction for procurement.
- If procurement is price-sensitive and can accept a short-term commitment, Dedicated Preview at $0.95/1M is defensible — we should push for a 3-month committed baseline equal to ~50% of expected pilot volume.
- Counterfactuals: if they compare to self-hosted open models, call out engineering TCO (ops, model upgrades, reliability). On our benchmarks, self-hosted can approach ~$0.50–0.70/1M but with heavy infra & headcount assumptions.

I'll draft a short two-option commercial that mirrors Ben's numbers and include one bullet on rollback/fallback (we can auto-fail to smaller model family if load exceeds the committed pool).

— Sergio
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Michael Trent <michael.trent@nimblehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jessica Lin <jessica.lin@nimblehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, procurement@nimblehealth.com
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: NimbleHealth discovery — unit economics & target $/1M

Irene / Ben / Sergio — thanks for the detailed breakdown. A couple clarifications from our side:

1) The 850M/mo steady-state is a mid-term projection; for the next 2 quarters we expect 200–400M/mo, with a pilot target right at 100M.
2) Procurement prefers a single pilot PO if the price is within reason; otherwise we need a short SOW. PO turnaround is typically 2–3 weeks.
3) Target unit economics for us to greenlight a pilot: ideally <= $1.00 / 1M tokens for the pilot footprint, or some hybrid (e.g., $1.50/1M hosted with a credit/volume rebate once we hit 400M).

Attached is the initial Q2 usage export. Happy to hop back on a quick call if you want to walk through the peaks and tail behavior.

-Michael
VP Product — NimbleHealth
[Attachment: nimble_q2_usage_export_from_nimble.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Trent <michael.trent@nimblehealth.com>, Jessica Lin <jessica.lin@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, procurement@nimblehealth.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: NimbleHealth discovery — unit economics & target $/1M

Thanks Michael — perfect, that helps a lot. Next steps from our side:

1) Ben / Sergio: please finalize the two-option commercial (Hosted Pilot @ $1.80/1M with a 10% pilot credit vs Dedicated Preview @ $0.95/1M with 3-month commit) but add a third negotiated hybrid option: Hosted $1.50/1M with a volume-rebate schedule kicking in at 400M/mo.
2) I'll prepare a short one-page pilot SOW (objectives, success metrics, termination, data handling) and loop in Legal for standard terms.
3) Michael / Procurement: once you confirm PO vs SOW preference, we'll send the commercial + SOW so procurement can start internal review.

I attached the redlined price comparison and our pilot SOW template to this reply. If you'd like a 20-minute sync to finalize the PO language, I have availability Thu 29 Apr 9–11am PT.

Appreciate it — talk soon.

Irene
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_price_comparison.pdf (PDF, updated)]
